exposure: radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy combined with caesarean section
cohort: This study included 19 pregnant women with early stage cervical cancer who underwent caesarean section combined with radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy, compared to 38 non-pregnant women who underwent radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy alone.
finding: Radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy combined with caesarean section in pregnant women with early stage cervical cancer resulted in higher estimated perioperative blood loss compared to non-pregnant women undergoing the procedure alone, but complication rates and oncological outcomes were similar between the two groups.
mod_finding: Neonatal survival rate was 100% in the group of pregnant women who underwent caesarean section combined with radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy.
who: Pregnant women with early stage cervical cancer and their babies
